item.title: Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
Police have opened a murder investigation following the death of a 61-year-old woman in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Alexandra Road at approximately 9:50pm yesterday evening, where the woman was found deceased. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the location on suspicion of murder and remains in custody.
Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee of the Major Crime Unit has described the event as an isolated incident and confirmed that police are not seeking any other suspects. Specialist officers remain at the scene to continue their enquiries. Anyone with information regarding the case is asked to contact the police via 101 or their website, quoting Operation Emeth.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Remembering a long-serving King’s Lynn factory worker
We take a look back at a long-standing career at the Campbell’s soup factory in King’s Lynn. In November 1996, Ken Durrant of Gaywood retired after 37 years of service. Mr Durrant was one of the first employees at the Hardwick Road site and spent 22 of those years working in the security hut. He was one of only two staff members to reach such a milestone at the company. Mr Durrant was joined by his wife and family for a farewell presentation with his colleagues to mark the end of his lengthy career.

item.description:

Safety improvements planned for West Lynn junction
Safety work is set to begin next month at the junction of Clenchwarton Road and the East Coast Business Park in West Lynn. Norfolk County Council is investing £16,500 to address a history of collisions at the site, with a specific focus on protecting cyclists.
Starting December 7, the two-week project will include new kerb build-outs, extended cycle paths, and updated signage. Temporary four-way traffic signals will be in operation throughout the works, which are subject to weather conditions. Local businesses requiring specific access arrangements are being asked to contact the highways department in advance. Further details regarding the project can be found on the Norfolk County Council website.

item.title: Birmingham teenager sentenced following Lynn nightclub incident
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Birmingham teenager sentenced following Lynn nightclub incident
A 19-year-old man from Birmingham has been handed a six-month conditional discharge after admitting to being drunk and disorderly in King’s Lynn. Brayden Tonks was arrested in the early hours of October 17 following a confrontation with door staff and police on Norfolk Street.
During the incident at 2:45am, Tonks swore at officers and behaved aggressively. Appearing before Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Tonks apologised for his actions and promised the court it would not happen again. In addition to the conditional discharge, he was ordered to pay £40 in court costs and a £26 victim surcharge.

King’s Lynn arts society reaches milestone with food bank donation
The Arts Society King’s Lynn has reached a significant milestone by donating its 1,000th art and craft pack to the town’s food bank. The project, which began in 2020, provides children from families using the food bank with creative materials and a reading book for Christmas. Each gift is presented in a handmade fabric bag, created with support from Norfolk Creative Arts and the Wootton Crafters.
Funding for this year’s packs was provided by local businesses and charities, including Mars Foods and Hayes and Storr Solicitors. Distribution of the gifts is scheduled to begin at the start of December. Food bank officials have expressed their gratitude for the ongoing support, noting the positive impact these donations have on local families.

item.title: Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
Norfolk County Council’s Health Overview Scrutiny Committee has examined a new ‘Case for Change’ report from the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group. The review outlines potential service adjustments at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, citing workforce shortages and a projected £53 million deficit by 2034.
Councillors raised concerns that proposed changes could force West Norfolk residents to travel to Norwich for care. During the meeting, Councillor Alexandra Kemp warned that longer travel times on the A47 could negatively impact patient outcomes. While no final decisions have been made, the committee has called for greater transparency and clarity regarding the potential impact on local families and the wider healthcare system.

item.title: Wisbech teenager disqualified for drink-driving
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech teenager disqualified for drink-driving
A 19-year-old woman from Wisbech has been banned from the roads after being caught drink-driving in King’s Lynn. Juste Kantautaite, of Southwell Road, was stopped by police on Blackfriars Road at 4:20am on October 18. Officers conducted a breath test after finding her stationary vehicle, which revealed she had 61mcg of alcohol in 100ml of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35mcg.
At Lynn Magistrates’ Court, the court heard that Kantautaite had been persuaded to drink while celebrating a friend’s birthday. She pleaded guilty to the offence and has been disqualified from driving for 17 months. In addition to the ban, she must pay a £400 fine, a £160 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

Hosted by West Norfolk Council, the free session connected businesses with organisations delivering major infrastructure schemes, including the new Queen Elizabeth Hospital and the West Winch access road.
Representatives from project teams, such as Skanska and Costain, provided details on procurement and future work packages. Attendees also received advice from support groups like the Norfolk Chamber of Commerce and the College of West Anglia. Councillor Simon Ring stated the event aims to help local companies understand how they can get involved in the area's ongoing investment projects.
